$comment: The deploy record's host table, in a form a program can check. README.md 'Hosting'
is the prose version of this file; when the two disagree this file is what runs.
Every host here is asserted on CONTENT, never on a status code. A host that
answers 200 while serving Bolt's 'Website Not Found' page is how the record
came to call a dead host healthy, so a 200 is never evidence on its own.
store        owner/repo of the markdown store, or a full git URL. Both are read
anonymously: no token, no secret, no credential helper.
storeRef     the branch the publish path is expected to have rendered. Written
down here because the deploy procedure says the expected head is
known, not inferred from a status code.
expect, per host:
build-info  GET <url>/build-info.json, require JSON with a 40-hex contentHead and a
non-empty siteTitle. requireCurrentStore additionally compares that
contentHead against the store's ref: equal passes, anything else fails.
The comparison is against the COMMIT, never against generated or
contentSyncedAt, because on 2026-10-05 two builds carried internally
consistent timestamps 17:08:15 and 17:40:46 while only one of them
matched the repository.
html        GET <url>/, require every string in `markers` and none in `forbidden`.
absent      GET <url>/, require that NONE of `markers` appear. For a host the record
knows is dead. Keeps the trap named in machine-readable form instead of
only in a commit message.

hosts.note: The verified publish path and the only URL a reader is given. Must be current.
Live and rebuilding, not the publish path. Staleness here is reported, not fatal, until BEL-199 decides whether the site is paused, removed, or kept in sync.
The interactive app: auth, comments, weather, admin. No markdown store, no sourcing gate, no feed.

Measured 2026-10-05: HTTP 200, 8478 bytes, body is Bolt's 'Website Not Found' page. Asserted dead on purpose so it cannot be re-recorded as healthy, and so a restored host is noticed instead of inherited.
